lens: I diffed the journal article, the tables file and the SI against their state several commits back (git log --oneline -25 -- <path>; git diff 34182cbf8 <pin> -- <path>, and 830679576 for the SI) and took every changed sentence back to the artifact it restates, then asked of each repair whether its sibling call sites moved with it. Concretely I re-derived, from research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json and aso_parent_gap_pairing.best_parent_duplex, that 'the longest is wild-type NR4A3' is the argmax predicate the field actually computes (87 liable, 61 argmax-NR4A3, 62 membership) and checked all three sites that print it; re-derived the scramble pair (aso-parent-null.json null_ensembles.scrambled_dinucleotide rate_liable 0.09987, rate_liable_attributed_to_NR4A3 0.03911 over n_draws 38000); confirmed from aso-genome-offtarget.json's denominator (windows_total 3,099,747,808, windows_with_N 151,138,112, windows_scanned 2,948,609,696) that 'unambiguous GRCh38' is the correct replacement for the deleted 'every position of GRCh38', and checked the sibling sentence in Results moved with it; recomputed the whole null comparison (panel Wilson intervals against the strongest of ten ensembles at every cut 6-13: inside at 7,8,9,10,12,13 and outside at 6 and 11 -> 'every cut from seven to thirteen but eleven' holds; excess sign changes at 6->7, 7->8, 9->10, 12->13 -> 'four times' holds); recomputed the power and voidness figures by simulation on the t interval (30.4% at three replicates, 81.3% at six; void sd* 0.6479 / 1.5336 / 2.2498 -> the printed 0.65, 1.53, 2.25); re-derived 176 distinct sequences, 9 at more than one junction, 85 own-parent, 38 junctions, FUS supplying 8, and the junction-availability ladder 6/9/23/31/35 and 0/0/2/3/5; verified the three-geometry series against aso-parent-gap-pairing-18mer-5-8-5.json (266/88) and -20mer-5-10-5.json (342/87); verified the reagents' 8 bp and 9 bp against wild-type TFG, the one-slide design's 11 bp against NR4A3, and the exon-2 pair's 8 bp EWSR1 / 9 bp NR4A3 from aso-parent-gap-pairing-noncoding-acceptor.json; verified the coverage arithmetic (0.5287+0.1552=68.4%, range 39.9-82.8%, third design 79.0%) against fusion-junction-aso-reagent-coverage.json; confirmed the DOI repoint 22182180 -> 22229096 reached every prose copy (both papers, deposit-state, cover letter, checklist) and that all four built PDFs carry the repaired sentences (pdfminer extraction; a first 'missing' reading of 'the top of the seven-to-ten' in two PDFs was line-break hyphenation, not staleness); and I mutation-tested the word-quantity bindings on a scratch copy of the article only. DISCLOSURES. (1) LEAKAGE: an early `git grep` scoped to the whole tree returned matching LINES from research/autonomy/review-seats/*.json, which are earlier seat records I was told not to read; I saw content from several, including a prior regression seat covering this same diff. I opened none of those files, every quantity I report I derived myself from the artifacts before or independently of that grep, and all later greps were scoped to research/manuscripts and research/modalities. The one finding that also appears there (the 3.9% denominator) is filed with that fact stated rather than dropped. (2) The pin was corrected twice mid-review (7d51f2051 -> 4bffe66a9 -> bc3741407); the article is byte-identical at all three and the intervening commits touch tooling and bookkeeping, so nothing I checked needed re-checking.
central_claim: Across a panel of 190 junction-spanning 5-6-5 gapmers tiled at 38 in-frame NR4A3 fusion junctions and put through five in-silico specificity screens, the binding constraint on a fusion-junction ASO for extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma is not designability but discrimination from the design's own wild-type parents: 87 of the 190 let a mature wild-type parent pair their whole catalytic gap over ten or more contiguous base pairs, the ten-base-pair cut is an adopted convention that exon-terminus chimeric nulls nearly match (40.6% against 45.8%), and what the work delivers is two named reagents at the two most-reported breakpoints, two screened controls, five candidate test articles and a pre-registrable selectivity threshold - with no efficacy, potency or safety claimed for any sequence.

p1s.summary: The parent-transcript count 'six' is printed at THREE sites and bound at two. The Results site - '87 let one of six mature wild-type parent transcripts pair their entire catalytic gap' - is reached by no guard and is not in the meta-guard's own record of deliberately unbound quantities, so the exact one-of-a-pair defect the round-31/32 word-quantity work was written to close survives at the third call site.
p1s.evidence: Sites, from the flattened article: (a) Methods, 'The fourth records the longest contiguous duplex any of six wild-type parent transcripts forms through the catalytic gap'; (b) Results line 206, 'Of those, 87 let one of six mature wild-type parent transcripts pair their entire catalytic gap...'; (c) Discussion line 347, 'the parent arm reads six transcripts'. The value is research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json method.parents_searched, which has 6 entries (EWSR1, FUS, NR4A3, TAF15, TCF12, TFG). Bindings: research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_journal_articles_word_quantities_are_derived.py:203 uses r'longest contiguous duplex any of (\w+) wild-type parent transcripts' (site a only), and research/manuscripts/tests/test_a_quantity_written_as_a_word_is_bound_too.py BINDINGS carries the same pattern for site (a) plus r'the parent arm reads (\w+) transcripts' labelled 'the mature screen's parent set, stated a second time' for site (c). No pattern in either file reaches site (b); the only other guard containing 'mature parents' is research/modalities/tests/test_aso_parent_gap_pairing.py, whose PAPER constant (lines 28-29) is fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md, a different document. Mutation-tested on a scratch copy of the article only (the live tree was not touched): replacing 'one of six mature wild-type parent transcripts' with 'one of ten mature wild-type parent transcripts' leaves all three regexes matching 'six' and every binding green. Reproduce: git show bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d:research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md | tr -s '[:space:]' ' ' | grep -o '[a-z]* mature wild-type parent transcripts'; then git grep -n 'wild-type parent transcripts' bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d -- research/manuscripts/tests/

p1s.summary: The article states the retrieved RNase-H1 working range twice. The Introduction's statement is DERIVED from the quoted source; the Results restatement ('the top of the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to prefer') is pinned as a literal string in the guard, so it is bound to its own spelling and not to the record. If the retrieved range ever moves, the Introduction can be corrected while the Results site keeps the stale number and both guards stay green.
p1s.evidence: Site 1, Introduction: 'Its length requirement is reported as a DNA gap of at least six nucleotides, with seven to ten the working range;<sup>13</sup><!--PMID:24981949-->'. This is derived: test_the_journal_articles_word_quantities_are_derived.py::test_the_rnase_h1_gap_lengths_are_the_retrieved_records_own reads research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-gap-length.json, extracts 'gap of (\w+) DNA nucleotides is necessary' and 'DNA gap size between (\d+) and (\d+) nucleotides is optimal' from the PMID 24981949 quotes, and compares the article to them. Site 2, Results: 'At 5-10-5 pairing the whole gap already demands ten base pairs, the top of the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to prefer, so a shorter run that could still license cleavage goes uncounted and that last figure is a floor'. Its only witness is research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py:1098, assert re.search(r'the top of the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to prefer', flat) - a literal, with no reference to lit-targets-aso-gap-length.json. Both numbers are correct at the pin: the record quotes 24981949 verbatim as 'a gap of six DNA nucleotides is necessary for noteworthy RNase H activity' and 'a DNA gap size between 7 and 10 nucleotides is optimal'. Reproduce: git show bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d:research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py | sed -n '1090,1100p'; git show bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d:research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-gap-length.json

p2s.summary: The 'floor' caveat is attached to one of three geometry rates by a reason that applies to all three. The repair replaced 'At 5-10-5 the criterion is met by the catalytic gap alone' with an argument - the criterion demands more paired bases than the enzyme is reported to need, so shorter licensing runs go uncounted - that is equally true at 5-6-5 and 5-8-5, yet only 'that last figure' is called a floor. A reader is left to infer that 45.8% and 33.1% are not floors.
p2s.evidence: The sentence: 'Across three geometries the liable count holds at 87, 88 and 87 while the panel grows from 190 designs to 266 and 342, so the rate falls from 45.8% to 33.1% and 25.4%: a longer gap buys margin per design without removing the liability. At 5-10-5 pairing the whole gap already demands ten base pairs, the top of the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to prefer, so a shorter run that could still license cleavage goes uncounted and that last figure is a floor.' All three screens run at the same absolute MIN_DUPLEX_BP of 10 (method.min_duplex_bp = 10 in aso-parent-gap-pairing.json, -18mer-5-8-5.json and -20mer-5-10-5.json), while the gaps are 6, 8 and 10 nt. So at 5-8-5 a window pairing the whole 8-nt gap with one flanking pair is 9 bp and goes uncounted although 8 nt sits inside the same source's 7-10 optimum; at 5-6-5 a fully paired 6-nt gap is 6 bp and goes uncounted although the same source is quoted for 'at least six nucleotides'. The artifacts say so themselves: _geometry._note in all three reads 'MIN_DUPLEX_BP is an ABSOLUTE hybrid length and does NOT scale with the gap... at a gap of 6 a window needs four further flanking pairs to reach it. Both readings are real and they are not the same reading.' Reproduce: for f in aso-parent-gap-pairing.json aso-parent-gap-pairing-18mer-5-8-5.json aso-parent-gap-pairing-20mer-5-10-5.json; do git show bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d:research/modalities/$f | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d["_geometry"]["architecture"], d["method"]["min_duplex_bp"], d["corpus"]["n_designs"], d["corpus"]["n_with_parent_duplex_through_gap"])'; done

p2s.summary: The repair gave the panel sentence and the controls sentence the same construction while their denominators differ: 61 is nested inside the 87, but 3.9% is a share of all 38,000 scramble draws rather than of the 10.0%. Both figures are right; the shared wording invites a reader to carry the nesting across and get both the number and the panel-versus-null comparison wrong.
p2s.evidence: Article line 206: 'Of those, 87 let one of six mature wild-type parent transcripts pair their entire catalytic gap over a contiguous duplex of at least ten base pairs, and for 61 of the 87 the longest is wild-type *NR4A3*' - nested. Article line 306-307: '10.0% of such scrambles pair a parent's whole catalytic gap at the ten-base-pair criterion, and for 3.9% the longest is wild-type *NR4A3*' - not nested. research/modalities/aso-parent-null.json null_ensembles.scrambled_dinucleotide gives n_draws 38000, rate_liable 0.09987 and rate_liable_attributed_to_NR4A3 0.03911, both over the same 38000, so the panel share is 61/87 = 70.1% of liable designs against 1486/3795 = 39.2% of liable scrambles - the two constructions are not the same statistic. Reproduce: git show bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d:research/modalities/aso-parent-null.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)["null_ensembles"]["scrambled_dinucleotide"]; print(d["n_draws"], d["n_liable"], d["rate_liable"], d["n_liable_against_NR4A3"], d["rate_liable_against_NR4A3"])'. p2s.summary: The provenance repair reached the article sentence and the tables page's own preamble and did not reach the generator's module docstring, which still asserts the superseded claim one screen above the comment that refutes it. The generator is a deposited file, so a reader who downloads the archive the paper cites finds a false provenance statement about the table they are ordering from.
p2s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso_journal_tables.py lines 17-20: 'THIS GENERATOR READS THE CANONICAL SEQUENCE FILE AND NOTHING ELSE, by design. Every cell it emits is a column of `fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv`... The one exception is the test-article map below.' The same file at lines 141-150 defines _controls(), which opens research/modalities/aso-control-oligos.json, and its own inline comment at ~line 201 says so: 'Table 2 does not come from that file at all - `_controls` reads `aso-control-oligos.json`. Nobody had noticed the last one in three rounds of getting this sentence wrong.' The emitted preamble at ~line 209 was repaired ('the reagents from `fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv`... and the controls from `aso-control-oligos.json`'), as was the article's Tables paragraph ('generated from the canonical sequence file and, for the controls, from the screened-control record it is itself built from'), which is itself accurate - aso_sequence_manifest.py:565 loads aso-control-oligos.json. Only the docstring was left. Reproduce: git show bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d:research/manuscripts/aso_journal_tables.py | sed -n '17,20p;141,150p'

p2s.summary: The 'every position of GRCh38' overstatement was corrected at both of its sites in the article and left standing in the deposited artifact's own summary fields and in the archive manifest that quotes them three times, so the deposit the paper cites still asserts the completeness the paper stopped asserting.
p2s.evidence: The article now reads 'The fifth covers unambiguous GRCh38, mitochondrial sequence included' (Methods) and 'It scans genomic sequence rather than transcripts' (Results), replacing 'covers every position of GRCh38' and 'It counts every position of GRCh38'. The correction is right: research/modalities/aso-genome-offtarget.json denominator gives windows_total 3,099,747,808, windows_with_N 151,138,112 and windows_scanned 2,948,609,696 (n_fraction 0.0488), i.e. 4.9% of windows are not scanned. But the same artifact's own _what still reads 'against every position of the reference genome' and method.completeness still reads 'definitional: every position is tested against the complete neighbourhood', and research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json repeats 'tested against every position of GRCh38' at lines 1861, 2833 and 5163. The extended report does disclose the exclusion ('windows containing an N were excluded, leaving 2,948,609,696 of 3,099,747,808'), so the deposit is not uniformly wrong - the artifact's summary fields are. Reproduce: git show bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d:research/modalities/aso-genome-offtarget.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d["_what"][:160]); print(d["method"]["completeness"][:160]); print({k:d["denominator"][k] for k in ("windows_total","windows_with_N","windows_scanned","n_fraction")})'; git grep -c 'every position of GRCh38' bc37414076b40d29139f6f02c78f9db3aed9ba1d -- research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json
